summary: Citizens of New Zealand's visa waiver countries and territories can visit for up to 3 months — 6 months for UK citizens — but must have an NZeTA before they travel, and most international visitors also pay the NZD 100 International Visitor Levy. Australian citizens need neither a visa nor an NZeTA, travellers on passports from some countries must apply for a Visitor Visa, and everyone travelling into New Zealand must complete a New Zealand Traveller Declaration; the declaration site suggests doing it before the flight, and for air travellers it needs to be submitted by the time they reach passport control.

declarations.submitWindow: By air: from 24 hours before you start your trip until you reach passport control in New Zealand. By sea: from 24 hours before departing the vessel’s last foreign port until it berths at its first New Zealand port.
declarations.text: Everyone travelling into New Zealand, including New Zealand passport holders, must complete the free New Zealand Traveller Declaration (website or app), which collects travel, customs, immigration and biosecurity information. Air travellers can submit it from 24 hours before they start their trip, and it needs to be submitted by the time they reach passport control in New Zealand; New Zealand Customs suggests doing it before the flight to make arrival easier. It is linked to your passport and checked at the eGate or by a border officer; you do not need to print anything.

overstay.text: Once a visa expires, the person is in New Zealand unlawfully, must leave immediately and is liable for deportation. A person deported for being unlawfully in New Zealand may not return for 2 years if deported not more than 12 months after becoming unlawful, and for 5 years if deported 12 months or more after, or if it is the second or subsequent time. No prohibition on entry applies to a person who leaves voluntarily before being served with a deportation order. Immigration New Zealand says a person may be banned from returning if they stay unlawfully for 42 days or more.

idp.text: New Zealand is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic (UN Treaty Collection). NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi says you can currently drive using an overseas car licence for up to 18 months from your last date of entry into New Zealand, and that from 1 November 2026 this will be reduced to 12 months from the day you last arrived. It says you can use an overseas motorcycle or truck licence for up to 12 months, that if your overseas licence isn't in English you must also have an accurate English translation or an international driving permit (IDP), and that you must also carry your current overseas licence.

tips.text: New Zealand's Ministry for Primary Industries says some foods, drinks, sports and outdoor equipment can carry harmful pests and diseases, and that if you're unsure you should declare your items when you arrive or put them in the bin, otherwise you can get a fine. The UK says it is illegal to import most food products, that tents, fishing equipment and golf clubs can carry pests, and that breaking the rules can mean a fine of up to NZ$100,000 or a prison sentence.

Complete the free New Zealand Traveller Declaration online or in the NZTD app: the declaration site suggests doing it before your flight to make arrival easier, says everyone travelling into New Zealand must complete one, and says it needs to be submitted by the time you reach passport control.

Canada says traffic drives on the left. The UK notes that highways can be narrow, winding and hilly, and Canada warns that rural railway crossings may have no barriers and that dairy herds often cross main roads at milking time.

Budget for the NZD 100 International Visitor Levy on top of the NZeTA fee (from NZD 17): the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment says most international visitors pay it when applying for a visa or NZeTA, and that it funds conservation, infrastructure used for tourism and other initiatives related to tourism.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for New Zealand?
faq.answer: Citizens of visa waiver countries need no visa, but must have an NZeTA before they travel (from NZD 17), and most international visitors also pay the NZD 100 International Visitor Levy. Immigration New Zealand says the NZeTA is valid for 2 years and allows stays of 3 months each visit. No official source we could read lists the visa waiver countries.

faq.question: How much does the NZeTA really cost?
faq.answer: Immigration New Zealand gives the NZeTA cost as from NZD 17 and explains how to request it using the online form or the app. The Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment says most international visitors also pay the NZD 100 International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL), when applying for a visa or NZeTA.

faq.question: Do Australians need an NZeTA or visa for New Zealand?
faq.answer: No. Immigration New Zealand says Australian citizens need neither a visa nor an NZeTA. It lists Australian permanent residents among the travellers who can visit New Zealand on an NZeTA.

faq.question: What is the New Zealand Traveller Declaration?
faq.answer: The NZTD is a free declaration that everyone travelling into New Zealand must complete, online at travellerdeclaration.govt.nz or in the NZTD app. It collects travel, customs, immigration and biosecurity information and replaces the old Passenger Arrival Card. New Zealand Customs suggests doing the digital declaration before your flight instead of filling in a paper declaration onboard; for air travellers it needs to be submitted by the time you reach passport control.

faq.question: How long can I stay in New Zealand as a visitor?
faq.answer: Immigration New Zealand says NZeTA visitors can stay up to 3 months each visit (6 months for UK citizens), and no more than 6 months within any 12-month period. It says a Visitor Visa lets you stay for up to either 6 or 9 months, with a maximum of 9 months in an 18-month period.

entryRequirements.declarations.nztd.text: It is FREE and everyone travelling into New Zealand must complete a declaration, including New Zealand passport holders.
The New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD) collects travel, customs, immigration and biosecurity information. It is free and you can do it on the online form or the NZTD app.
The earliest you can submit your declaration is 24 hours before you start your trip to New Zealand. It needs to be submitted by the time you reach passport control in New Zealand.
To make your arrival easier do your digital declaration before your flight to New Zealand, instead of filling in a paper declaration onboard.

You do not need to print anything out. Your declaration will automatically be checked at passport control when you scan your passport at the eGate or when it is checked by a border officer on arrival into New Zealand.

Note Your onward tickets must be paid for before your travel. If you will be leaving on a private craft or cruise ship, we will accept a letter from the craft owner or a cruise itinerary as proof of your travel arrangements.
They may also ask to see your ticket for travel out of New Zealand at the end of your visit.
